australium.footer: Solve these assignments to receive Moustachium alloy in TF2 and craft fantastic SpaceChem items!
reactor.waldo.heading: heading {dir}
tut.ex1.welcome: Tutorial. Welcome to SpaceChem. {repeat} repeats a tutorial step at any time. You're on the reactor grid, 10 columns by 8 rows; cells are read column first, then row, counting from 1, 1 at the top left. You never move atoms yourself: two waldos, robotic arms, one red and one blue, travel the grid and run the instructions of their own colour. This level needs only the red one. Press {jumpRed} to jump to where it starts.
tut.ex1.welcome.after: This is the red waldo's start. When the reactor runs, the waldo sets off the way its start points, left here, and keeps going until an instruction turns it or it runs into the side of the reactor, where it stops.
tut.ex1.start: The tutorial's steps are laid out around the red start at {cell}, pointing left; put it back there to follow along. A start can't be deleted, only moved: {cut} on it, then {paste} on {cell}. If it points another way, {valueNext} on it turns it.
tut.ex1.alpha: To the start's left lies the alpha input zone. Arrow left until you're in it.
tut.ex1.alpha.after: This is the alpha input, columns 1 to 4, rows 1 to 4: the square where new molecules arrive. The beta input is the square below it. Columns 5 and 6 are the chamber, and on the right are the outputs, psi on top and omega below, where finished molecules leave the reactor. The grid names each zone as you cross into it.
tut.ex1.viewer: To see what this input brings, press {molecule} on any cell of the zone.
tut.ex1.viewer.after: This is the molecule viewer. It lays the molecule out on the reactor cells where it will land, with your cursor on its first atom. Each cell reads its atom and its bonds, and the arrows move between them.
tut.ex1.viewer.close: Look around, then press {back} to close the viewer.
tut.ex1.viewer.close.after: So alpha brings two oxygen atoms, landing at 2, 2 and 3, 2, joined by a double bond: one oxygen molecule, O2. Bonds matter later; for now, when a waldo moves one atom, everything bonded to it comes along.
tut.ex1.psi: What does this reactor have to make? Press {psi} to hear what the psi output wants.
tut.ex1.psi.after: Psi wants 10 molecules of oxygen, O2, the very molecule alpha brings. So the job is to take each one in, carry it to psi and send it out, again and again. You do that with instructions: they sit on cells, and a waldo runs the ones of its own colour as it passes over them. Letter keys place them at the cursor in the active colour, red for now. From here on the tutorial asks for exact cells, and the one it wants reads highlighted. That's only so it can follow along: where things go is up to you. An input works anywhere on the waldo's path, not just in its zone, starts can be moved, and there's more than one way to solve any level.
tut.ex1.input: The waldo leaves its start heading left, so the first cell it reaches is {cell}. Go there and press {key} to place an input: each time the waldo passes it, a new molecule appears in the alpha zone, right where the viewer showed it.
tut.ex1.input.after: Placing an instruction reads it back. {delete} removes the red instruction under the cursor and Ctrl+Z undoes; take away one the tutorial asked for and it asks for it again.
tut.ex1.grab: Still heading left, the waldo reaches {cell} next, where the new molecule's right-hand oxygen lands. Place a grab drop there with {key}. Passing it with nothing in hand, the waldo grabs the atom under it, and the molecule comes with it.
tut.ex1.down: Holding the molecule and still going left, the waldo would push the left-hand oxygen into the reactor's side, and an atom hitting the side or another atom stops the reactor with an error. Turn it: an arrow down at {cell}, key {key}. Arrows change the waldo's direction.
tut.ex1.right: Two rows down is far enough. Place an arrow right at {cell} with {key}; the waldo will head right, through the chamber toward psi. A cell holds one arrow and one other instruction of each colour, and the waldo runs the instruction first, then the arrow.
tut.ex1.rotate: This one is only for demonstration; the solution works without it. Place a rotate counter-clockwise at {cell} with {key}. When the waldo passes it holding a molecule, the molecule turns a quarter turn to the left, around the atom the waldo holds.
tut.ex1.up: Past the rotation, the second oxygen hangs below the waldo, in row 5, which is omega's. Place an arrow up at {cell} with {key}, so the whole molecule moves up into psi. Without a turn the waldo would also run into the right side and stop.
tut.ex1.left: Now head back: an arrow left at {cell}, key {key}. A reactor program is a loop, run over and over, one molecule each lap, so the waldo has to return to the input.
tut.ex1.drop: A molecule is delivered only when it lies entirely inside the output zone and nobody holds it. Place a grab drop at {cell} with {key}: the waldo arrives holding the molecule, so here it lets go.
tut.ex1.output: Last instruction: an output at {cell}, key {key}. When the waldo passes it, every molecule lying loose in psi leaves the reactor and counts toward the 10. Then the waldo carries on left to the input, and the next lap begins.
tut.ex1.trace: The program is complete. Before running it, hear its route: press {traceRed} for the red waldo's path, every cell where it does something, in order.
tut.ex1.trace.close: Up and Down walk the path, and Enter on a line jumps the cursor to its cell. Close it with {back}.
tut.ex1.step: Time to run it, one event at a time. Press {step}: the reactor runs until something happens, a molecule coming in, a grab, a turn, a waldo hitting a wall, then pauses and says what happened.
tut.ex1.step.after: Between steps the reactor holds still: arrow around the grid to find the waldo and the atoms where they are. The blue waldo runs too, but with no blue instructions it just heads left until it hits the wall.
tut.ex1.run: Keep pressing {step} to follow a molecule all the way into psi. When you've seen enough, press 1 to run at the slowest speed with every event spoken, or 4 for the fastest. Psi needs 10 molecules to finish the level, and every event of a run goes to the Run log, the last Tab stop.
tut.t1.welcome: Tutorial. This time the red waldo has the day off and the blue one does the work. The blue waldo behaves exactly like the red one, but it runs only blue instructions; each waldo ignores the other colour's. Press {jumpBlue} to jump to the blue waldo's start.
tut.t1.welcome.after: The blue start, pointing left. Starts can't be deleted, but they can be moved: {cut} on a start, then {paste} on the cell you want it in. The tutorial's steps are laid out around this one, so leave it here for now.
tut.t1.start: The tutorial's steps are laid out around the blue start at {cell}, pointing left; put it back there to follow along: {cut} on it, then {paste} on {cell}. If it points another way, {valueNext} on it turns it.
tut.t1.beta: To its left lies the beta input. Arrow left into it.
tut.t1.beta.after: The beta input, columns 1 to 4, rows 5 to 8, right under alpha.
tut.t1.viewer: Press {molecule} to see what it brings.
tut.t1.viewer.close.after: Hydrogen, H2: two hydrogen atoms, landing at 2, 6 and 3, 6, joined by a single bond.
tut.t1.omega: Press {omega} to hear what the omega output wants.
tut.t1.skip: Arrows move one cell at a time. {skipUp}, {skipDown}, {skipLeft} and {skipRight} skip over cells that read the same and stop at the first one that differs, and crossing into another zone stops them too, so an empty stretch goes by in one press. Try one.
tut.t1.input.place: Now to build. The blue waldo heads left from its start, so the first cell it reaches is {cell}, and that's where the input goes. Go there and press {key}. Letter keys place instructions in the active colour, still red, so you'll get a red alpha input. You'll change both next.
tut.t1.input.place.blue: The blue waldo heads left from its start, so the first cell it reaches is {cell}, and that's where the input goes. Go there and press {key}: with blue active, it places a blue beta input.
tut.t1.input.colour: Every instruction has settings, called parameters: its colour, and for an input, which input it takes. On its cell, {paramPrev} and {paramNext} walk its parameters, and {valuePrev} and {valueNext} change the one you're on. You start on its colour: press {valueNext} to make it blue.
tut.t1.input: It's blue now, but it still takes alpha. Press {paramNext} to reach its input type, then {valueNext} to make it beta. Quicker still: {primaryPrev} and {primaryNext} change an instruction's main parameter, the input type here, whatever parameter you're on.
tut.t1.input.after: If you'd rather see every setting at once, {menu} on a cell opens its menu, the game's right-click, with a row per parameter.
tut.t1.layer: Changing the colour of every instruction gets old fast. New instructions take the active colour, and it's still red: press {layer} to switch it to blue.
tut.t1.layer.after: Everything you place is blue from now on, and the inputs and outputs you place take beta and omega. {layer} switches back.
tut.t1.up: Past the input the waldo reaches {cell}. Place an arrow up there with {key}, toward the row the hydrogen lands in.
tut.t1.right: At {cell}, one row up, turn it right with {key}, into the hydrogen's row. Either waldo can go anywhere in the reactor and use every input and output: red simply starts at the top and blue at the bottom.
tut.t1.grab: Last one: a grab drop at {cell}, key {key}, where the right-hand hydrogen lands.
tut.t1.grab.after: You got it! We'll let you finish the rest of the level like the good corporate drone you are: drop the hydrogen into the omega output zone and send it out. {traceBlue} reads the blue waldo's path, and {step} steps through a run, as on the last level.
